summary:
The **SPHEREx Explorer** is an interactive web platform designed to facilitate access to and exploration of astronomical data from NASA's SPHEREx mission. It allows users to search celestial regions using Right Ascension and Declination coordinates, visualize observations across different dates, and explore changes over time.

The platform integrates interactive sky maps, observation maps, wavelength and detector filters, spectral analysis, temporal image visualization, and an image gallery. It also includes an accessible glossary of astronomical terms to support users in understanding scientific concepts.

The project aims to make astronomical data more accessible by transforming complex scientific information into an intuitive, visual, and educational experience. By reducing technical barriers, SPHEREx Explorer contributes to science communication, supports astronomical learning, and encourages public engagement with space exploration.
details:
SPHEREx Explorer is an interactive web platform developed to facilitate the exploration, visualization, and interpretation of astronomical data from NASA's SPHEREx mission. Users can search celestial regions using astronomical coordinates (Right Ascension and Declination), define the field of view (FOV), and visualize observations from different dates to track changes in the same region of the sky.

The platform provides temporal image visualization, wavelength and detector filters, an interactive sky map, an observation map, spectral analysis, and an image gallery. It also includes a glossary of astronomical terms with simplified explanations, making the experience accessible to students, researchers, and astronomy enthusiasts.

The project uses HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the frontend, integrated with a Python backend developed using FastAPI. It also incorporates Aladin Lite for interactive sky visualization and astronomical data services such as IRSA/IPAC, CDS, Gaia DR3, and AllWISE.

Its creative aspect lies in integrating different scientific tools into a single platform, transforming complex astronomical data into an interactive and educational experience. Key development considerations included accessibility, intuitive navigation, responsiveness, coordinate validation, scientific data reliability, and clarity of information.

The intended impact is to democratize access to astronomical data, encourage scientific learning, and bring space exploration closer to society.
